## project

本项目拟利用小鼠小肠类器官培养体系，在太空环境与地面环境下对比小肠隐窝分化形成类器官的规律，并从线粒体DNA类核形态、mtDNA损伤、线粒体ROS和钙信号等亚细胞层面，研究太空环境对小肠线粒体稳态的作用机制。项目依托中国空间站已有载荷实施，实验周期覆盖地面方法建立（2023年）、镜像装置调试（2024年）和在轨实验及返回后分析（2025年）。[@E4][@E6][@E12][@E13][@E14][@E15][@E20][@E21][@E34]

## scope

本次评价依据完整项目计划书（sample2）及两份外部公开摘要——Marotta等（2023）人iPSC来源神经类器官ISS培养研究，Mair等（2024）心脏芯片平台空间飞行研究。研究工具已关闭；外部资料仅有摘要，正文方法、统计比较和图表未读。评价基于已读材料的实际覆盖面形成判断，不宣称已研究原文方法和图表。[@E40][@E41]

## unknowns

### 安全性分析与工程实施细节

申请中风险分析部分仅陈述"项目方案成熟、稳定，无技术风险"，未对生物材料与荧光染料在轨操作的密封、泄漏处置及废物管理进行具体分析。这些条件未确定，但现有材料也未揭示具体的危险事实。[@E30][@E20][@E21]

### 太空辐射与微重力效应的区分

项目科学问题同时提及"太空微重力环境"和"太空辐射"，但实验设计以地面对照与在轨实验对比为主，未描述辐射剂量监测或屏蔽对照等可区分两类因素的手段。辐射对mtDNA损伤的归因在现有设计中缺乏独立的因果识别条件。[@E15][@E13][@E6]

### 地面预实验的完成状态

年度计划表将地面方法建立列为2023年目标、镜像装置调试列为2024年目标，申请中未呈现已完成的地面预实验数据。研究基础主要依赖承担单位的实验室平台条件，而非已取得的项目相关实验结果。[@E34][@E28]

### 外部先例的适用范围

两份外部摘要——Marotta等（2023）神经类器官ISS实验和Mair等（2024）心脏芯片空间实验——仅以摘要形式获取。前者验证了类器官空间培养及返回后多组学分析的可行性，后者展示了在轨实时监测与线粒体相关改变的检测路径。但两者均为不同组织类型和不同实验平台，不能直接替代本项目小鼠小肠类器官与mtDNA类核成像的具体方法验证。[@E40][@E41]

## safety_veto

安全否决 applies：false

本项目涉及小鼠小肠组织、Matrigel基质胶、以及pico-green、TMRM/mito-tracker-green、DCF、Fluo8等荧光染料。这些均为常规生物实验室试剂，未涉及易燃易爆、剧毒或放射性物质。申请未具体描述在轨密封、泄漏处置和废物管理方案，但现有材料未揭示影响航天员或平台安全的具体危险路径。因此不触发安全一票否决。[@E20][@E21]

evidence-ba5eec447b34e6e7.title: sample2
evidence-ba5eec447b34e6e7.quote: 小肠干细胞维持肠道稳态、保护肠道屏障，越来越多的研究发现线粒体调控小肠的稳态。我们利用肠类器官培养体系揭示太空环境与地面环境下小肠类器官形成的差异规律，研究太空环境下小鼠小肠细胞 mtDNA 类核相分离、mtDNA 损伤情况、线粒体 ROS 和钙信号的变化，揭示太空环境对小肠线粒体稳态的作用机制，可望降低航天员因航空航天中线粒体变化而产生的不良反应。

evidence-26ad7e1954ac19f3.title: sample2
evidence-26ad7e1954ac19f3.quote: （1）地面环境下，观察小鼠小肠隐窝分化成小肠类器官过程中小肠类器官的大小与管腔数目，检测小肠细胞线粒体 DNA 类核形态、线粒体DNA 损伤以及线粒体钙、氧等信号。 （2）太空环境下，确定鼠小肠隐窝分化成小肠类器官过程中小肠类器官的大小与管腔数目，检测小肠细胞线粒体的 DNA 类核形态、线粒体DNA 损伤以及线粒体钙、氧等信号。通过地面环境下的对照实验，确定太空环境对小肠类器官形成的影响，以及对小肠细胞线粒体 DNA 和线粒体信号的作用规律； 2、项目年度目标及考核指标（表 2，考核指标包括项目的科学指标、关键技术指标，以及发表论文、专利、人才培养等）；

evidence-6ab014f0347920a8.title: sample2
evidence-6ab014f0347920a8.locator: （1）太空环境与地面环境对比小肠类器官的形成规律 / p12
evidence-6ab014f0347920a8.quote: 首先在地面环境下，观察小肠隐窝分化成小肠类器官过程中小肠类器官的大小与管腔数目，然后通过地面镜像装置调试小肠隐窝培养条件和普通明场成像适配，最后在太空环境下观察小肠隐窝分化成小肠类器官过程中小肠类器官的大小与管腔数目。通过与地面环境的数据对比，研究太空环境对小肠类器官形成的影响。

evidence-14a1620da6dc8b3e.title: sample2
evidence-14a1620da6dc8b3e.locator: （2）太空环境与地面环境对小肠细胞线粒体 DNA 类核影响 / p13
evidence-14a1620da6dc8b3e.quote: 首先在地面环境下，通过荧光成像检测小肠细胞线粒体 DNA 类核形态，通过线粒体 DNA 全长 PCR 扩增和二代测序检测线粒体 DNA 突变率。然后通过地面镜像装置调试小肠细胞线粒体 DNA 类核的成像参数，最后在太空环境下通过荧光成像检测小肠细胞线粒体 DNA 类核形态。地面返回小肠细胞样品后，通过少量细胞线粒体 DNA 全长 PCR 扩增，检测线粒体 DNA 突变率。通过与地面环境的数据对比，研究太空环境下小肠细胞线粒体的 DNA 类核和线粒体 DNA 损伤的作用。

evidence-2a335b7fa03f3c59.title: sample2
evidence-2a335b7fa03f3c59.locator: （3）太空环境对小肠细胞的线粒体信号影响 / p14
evidence-2a335b7fa03f3c59.quote: 首先在地面环境下，通过荧光成像检测小肠细胞线粒体 ROS 和钙信号，然后通过地面镜像装置调试小肠细胞线粒体 ROS 和钙信号成像参数。最后在太空环境下通过荧光成像检测小肠细胞线粒体 ROS 和钙信号。通过与地面环境的数据对比，研究太空环境对小肠细胞线粒体 ROS 和钙信号的影响。

evidence-f4b37a104c7e1cdd.locator: 2、拟重点解决的科学问题 / p15
evidence-f4b37a104c7e1cdd.quote: 揭示太空微重力环境对小肠隐窝分化成小肠类器官的作用，阐述太空微重力环境对线粒体 DNA 类核形态和线粒体信号的影响，并明确太空辐射对线粒体基因

evidence-8384b3a6dfd9b3de.title: Studies on the International Space Station to assess the effects of microgravity on iPSC-derived neural organoids
evidence-8384b3a6dfd9b3de.quote: Abstract Exposure to microgravity in low-Earth orbit (LEO) has been shown to affect human cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, and immune systems. Post-flight brain imaging indicates that reports about astronauts and mouse models suggest that microgravity may cause intracranial fluid shifts and possibly alter white and gray matter of the brain [1]. To focus on the effects of microgravity on the brain, we used induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) to produce three-dimensional (3D) human neural organoids as models of the nervous system. We studied iPSCs derived from four individuals, including people with the neurological diseases primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS) and Parkinson’s disease (PD) and non-symptomatic controls. We patterned the organoids toward cortical and dopaminergic fates representing regions of the brain affected by MS and PD, respectively. Microglia were generated from the same cell lines and integrated into a portion of the organoids. The organoids were maintained for 30 days in a novel static culture system on the International Space Station (ISS) and live samples were returned to Earth. The post-flight samples were evaluated using histology, transcriptome and secretome analysis. Microglia-specific genes and secreted proteins were detectable in the microglia-containing organoid cultures. The gene expression analyses of individual organoids cultured in LEO and on Earth suggest that cell proliferation was lower and neural cells were more mature in samples that were cultured in LEO. These experiments lay the groundwork for further studies, including long term studies to investigate the effects of microgravity on the brain. With two more missions using similar cells, we are determining whether this effect of microgravity is consistent in separate experiments. Such studies may ultimately aid in developing countermeasures for the effects of microgravity on the nervous systems of astronauts during space exploration and suggest novel therapeutic interventions for neurological diseases on Earth.

evidence-5843aa5489150d15.title: Spaceflight-induced contractile and mitochondrial dysfunction in an automated heart-on-a-chip platform.
evidence-5843aa5489150d15.quote: With current plans for manned missions to Mars and beyond, the need to better understand, prevent, and counteract the harmful effects of long-duration spaceflight on the body is becoming increasingly important. In this study, an automated heart-on-a-chip platform was flown to the International Space Station on a 1-mo mission during which contractile cardiac function was monitored in real-time. Upon return to Earth, engineered human heart tissues (EHTs) were further analyzed with ultrastructural imaging and RNA sequencing to investigate the impact of prolonged microgravity on cardiomyocyte function and health. Spaceflight EHTs exhibited significantly reduced twitch forces, increased incidences of arrhythmias, and increased signs of sarcomere disruption and mitochondrial damage. Transcriptomic analyses showed an up-regulation of genes and pathways associated with metabolic disorders, heart failure, oxidative stress, and inflammation, while genes related to contractility and calcium signaling showed significant down-regulation. Finally, in silico modeling revealed a potential link between oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction that corresponded with RNA sequencing results. This represents an in vitro model to faithfully reproduce the adverse effects of spaceflight on three-dimensional (3D)-engineered heart tissue.
